originalTitle: SIF AUM jumps 29% to Rs 17,858 crore in June; inflows surge 171% MoM
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the news: Specialised Investment Funds (SIF) had a big increase in the amount of money they managed, with a 29% jump to Rs 17,858 crore in June. This happened because a lot more money was put into these funds, with a 171% increase from the previous month. A type of fund called Hybrid Long-Short Funds was particularly popular. This is a good sign for the overall mutual fund industry, which also saw many investors participating. This trend suggests that regular investors, like individuals, are continuing to show interest in investing in the stock market.

originalTitle: DMart Q1 results: Cons PAT up 11% to Rs 860 crore, revenue rises to Rs 18,795 crore
simplifiedContent: DMart, a retail company, recently released its financial results for the first quarter of the year. The company's profit increased by 11.3% to Rs 860 crore, which means it made more money compared to the same time last year. Its revenue, or the total amount of money it made from sales, also went up by 14.9%. This increase in profit and revenue is a positive sign for the company, and its operating efficiency also improved slightly. This matters because it shows how well the company is doing and can affect its stock price and investor confidence.

originalTitle: Nearly 60% of foreign inflows into India-focused funds withdrawn since 2024 peak: Report
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: foreign investors who had put money into funds that focus on India's stock market have taken out almost 60% of that money since 2024. This means they're no longer investing as much in India's stock market as they used to. Instead, they're putting their money into other investments, like companies that work with artificial intelligence, which seems to be a popular choice right now. In 2026, about $9 billion was withdrawn from India-focused funds, which is a significant amount of money. This matters because it can affect the overall performance of India's stock market and the companies listed on it.

originalTitle: Nomura sees 22% upside in Ather Energy. Here's why it's the brokerage's top EV pick
simplifiedContent: Nomura, a company that helps people decide what stocks to buy, thinks Ather Energy is a good investment and predicts its stock price will go up by 22%. They believe this because they think many people will start buying electric two-wheelers, like scooters, instead of traditional gas-powered ones. As a result, Nomura has raised its target price for Ather Energy to ₹1,470 and is telling people to buy the stock. This is important because it means Nomura thinks Ather Energy will do well financially and its stock price will increase. Nomura likes Ather Energy so much that it's their top pick for electric vehicle companies.

originalTitle: Why large cap and mid cap funds could be the best mutual fund to bet on now, according to Abakkus study
simplifiedContent: A recent study by Abakkus Mutual Fund suggests that large and mid-sized company funds might be a good investment choice right now. This is because company earnings are improving and the prices of these funds are reasonable. The stock market has recently gone down, which means it could be a good time for long-term investors to get in. This is because the lower prices might give investors a chance to buy into funds that could grow in value over time as company earnings increase. Overall, this could be a good opportunity for investors to consider large and mid-sized company funds.

originalTitle: AI chip fever returns? SK Hynix  share price surges 13% after blockbuster $26.5 billion US listing
simplifiedContent: SK Hynix, a company that makes computer chips, just listed its shares on the US stock market and it was very successful, raising $26.5 billion. The company's share price jumped up 13% on the first day, which is a big increase. This is notable because the stock market for semiconductor companies like SK Hynix has been a bit unpredictable lately. The strong interest in SK Hynix's shares suggests that investors are excited about companies that make chips for artificial intelligence (AI) technology. This is because AI is a growing area and companies need good computer chips to support it, which is driving up demand and prices for these chips.
